The message is stored on this phone first and sent automatically as soon as a network is available. You can cancel it while it is queued. FloodCue only reports that the message left this device — whether it arrives depends on your carrier.
To send it automatically, FloodCue needs the SMS permission. If you do not grant it, FloodCue will open your SMS app instead and you press Send there yourself.

You can prepare this SOS without internet. Sending an SMS still needs a working cellular SMS service.
Tip: for the fastest emergency sending, set FloodCue battery usage to Unrestricted — Settings → Apps → FloodCue → Battery.
SOS stored on this phone. It will be sent automatically as soon as a network is available.
SOS queued. It will be sent automatically as soon as this phone has mobile signal — SMS travels over the mobile network, not Wi‑Fi.
Last send attempt failed: no mobile network. SMS needs mobile signal (SIM + network), not an internet/Wi‑Fi connection. The SOS keeps retrying automatically as soon as signal returns.
Last send attempt failed: the mobile radio is off — check airplane mode. The SOS retries automatically once it is back on.
The last send attempt failed. The message stays queued and retries automatically.
No SIM card detected in this phone — SMS cannot be sent without one.
